sheet-3-1.description: The main map of sheet 3 covers the northern half of the planned resort of Interlaken, drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It runs from Rona Street, which sweeps in a broad curve along the northern edge of the development, south to Scarba Street at the foot of the sheet, where it adjoins sheet 4. The streets form a regular grid of long, narrow blocks: Windemere, Grasmere, Bendermere, Buttermere and Bridlemere Avenues run down the page, crossed by Barra Street and Scarba Street. In the east Rona Street turns south as a separate avenue and an unnamed curving street loops around a large open tract before running down toward Deal Lake. Deal Lake, tinted blue, bounds the map on the west, where the lots of blocks 17 and 27 run down to an irregular shore with small inlets, and appears again in the south-east corner beside Bridlemere Avenue. The map is a subdivision plan rather than a built-up district: every block is cut into numbered building lots (numbers in the 270s to 470s) and block numbers 17 to 27 are printed, but no buildings are drawn in this part. Street widths of 40 and 65 feet are lettered at the corners. A dashed paper street continues Grasmere Avenue north beyond Rona Street toward the inset boxes. The scale bar is printed in Scarba Street at the bottom, and the top of the sheet is taken up by two insets of other places, which are separate parts.
notes: Windemere Avenue is Windermere Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Grasmere Avenue is Grassmere Avenue.
The curving street in the east is lettered only 'Street'; it lies on today's Bridlemere Avenue and Woodmere Avenue alignments.
No buildings are drawn: the part shows the lot plan of the development.
North arrow points about 7 to 10 degrees off true north (magnetic).

Interlaken north half, 120 ft to an inch: Rona, Barra, Scarba Streets; Windemere, Grasmere, Bendermere, Buttermere, Bridlemere Avenues; Deal Lake on the west. Three parts: 1 main map; 2 inset top left (Sunset Avenue at Deal Lake, wooden bridge, pavilion; same 120 ft scale, Wanamassa side of the lake); 3 inset top right at 60 ft to an inch (Roseld Avenue and Stratford Place, Deal; 'this section also shown on Vol. 1 N.J.C.M.'). North arrows point to magnetic north (about 10 degrees off).

sheet-3-2.description: This inset in the upper left corner of sheet 3, boxed by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale of 120 feet to an inch, shows the end of Sunset Avenue at Deal Lake on the Wanamassa side of the lake, west of Interlaken. Sunset Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs down the inset from the top edge, crosses an unnamed 60-foot street lettered only 'Street', and ends at the shore of Deal Lake, which crosses the lower left of the inset as a blue band. From the end of the avenue a wooden bridge, lettered as 320 feet long, crosses the lake diagonally toward the lower left; this is the forerunner of today's Sunset Avenue bridge. East of Sunset Avenue, at the corner of the cross street, is a small two-storey dwelling labelled The Pines, with an open first storey. Further east, in a large open tract, stands a pavilion of steel frame construction with a two-storey frame building attached. The rest of the inset is blank, without lot lines. A block number 38 is printed on the west side, beside the lake, and the inset has its own north arrow, pointing to the upper right. The inset was evidently added to the Interlaken sheets to record the lake pavilion and the bridge, which lie outside the area of the sheets.
notes: The cross street is not named on the sheet; it was identified as today's Camp Avenue (Ocean Township) from its position 300 ft from the lake shore and its angle to Sunset Avenue. Low confidence.
Placed from one detected junction (Sunset Avenue / Camp Avenue) with the scale of the main map and rotation from the drawn street lines.
Wooden bridge across Deal Lake, 320 ft long; pavilion of steel frame; dwelling 'The Pines'.

sheet-3-3.description: This inset fills the upper right of sheet 3 inside a heavy border and is drawn at a larger scale, 60 feet to an inch, with a note that the section is also shown on volume 1 of the New Jersey Coast maps. It shows part of Deal, east of Interlaken near the ocean, around the junction of Roseld Avenue and Stratford Place. Roseld Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs down the inset just left of centre; Stratford Place comes in from the left and ends at it, with a fire hydrant on the corner. Block 17 occupies the corner north of Stratford Place, with a further lot below. East of Roseld Avenue lies a large estate of several lots drawn with only their outlines. Its buildings are a large two-storey frame dwelling near the top, a long stable or barn and an outbuilding in the middle, and a group of service buildings lower down: a two-storey wagon house, a two-storey laundry and a small octagonal ice house, with another large two-and-a-half-storey dwelling near the bottom. Buildings are lettered A to G for the key. The inset has its own north arrow toward the upper right and its own scale note; the rest of the area is blank paper.
notes: Drawn at 60 ft to an inch, twice the scale of the rest of the sheet.
Placed from one detected junction (Roseld Avenue / Stratford Place) with the configured scale and rotation from the drawn street lines. Low confidence.
Estate with wagon house, laundry and ice house on the east side of Roseld Avenue.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 covers the southern half of Interlaken at 120 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. This part runs from Scarba Street at the top, where it adjoins sheet 3, south to the shore of Deal Lake. Windemere, Grasmere, Bendermere, Buttermere and Bridlemere Avenues run down the page, crossed by Westra, Staffa and Iona Streets, and Windemere Avenue curves east into the line of Iona Street at its south end. Most blocks are divided into numbered building lots (block numbers 1 to 17) with only scattered buildings: a few frame dwellings and a small pump house of the water works on Grasmere Avenue at Westra Street. Most of the houses stand in the southern blocks between Iona Street and Bridlemere Avenue, which follows the lake shore as a curving road with dashed water pipes. Deal Lake wraps around the west side, with its inlets and a boat house at the end of Windemere Avenue, and around the south and east; west of Grasmere Avenue's extension a large open tract is lettered Hotel Site. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn along Grasmere Avenue and Bridlemere Avenue. On the east side, across the lake and reached by Westra Street on a bridge, is part of West Allenhurst: Edgemere Drive along the lake, Staffa Street and Beachwood Avenue, with block 2.
notes: Windemere Avenue is Windermere Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Grasmere Avenue is Grassmere Avenue; Edgemere Drive is South Edgemere Drive; Beachwood Avenue is Beechwood Avenue.
Hotel site lettered west of the Grasmere Avenue extension; boat house at the end of Windemere Avenue; pump house on Grasmere Avenue.
The railroad and the Allenhurst blocks south of Deal Lake are drawn about 22 m out of place relative to the Interlaken streets; they are a separate part (sheet 4, part 2).

Interlaken south half, 120 ft to an inch: Scarba, Westra, Staffa, Iona Streets; Windemere to Bridlemere Avenues; Deal Lake; West Allenhurst strip on the east (Edgemere Drive, Allenhurst Avenue, Staffa Street); New York and Long Branch Railroad, passenger station and part of Allenhurst (Lake Drive, Elberon Avenue, Main Street) along the bottom. One part.

sheet-4-2.description: This part is the strip along the bottom of sheet 4, south of Deal Lake, drawn at 120 feet to an inch. It is cut off from the Interlaken streets at the lake shore because it is drawn about 22 metres out of place against them and is placed on its own control. The New York and Long Branch Railroad crosses the whole width as a band of several tracks, with the passenger station (a one-storey frame building with a stone section) on its south side near the left, and an East Jersey Coast Company line laid in 1898 is noted along its north side. Below the tracks Deal Lake's southern arms run down to the bottom edge, crossed by a wooden bridge and a street railway bridge. A large water pipe crosses from the north along the line of Grasmere Avenue, and a 6-inch pipe laid in 1898 runs south. To the east are blocks of Allenhurst: Lake Drive along the lake shore north of the railroad and again diagonally south of it, Elberon Avenue, Allen Avenue at the right edge and Main Street along the bottom, with the key number 5 for the adjoining sheet. The blocks are drawn as outlines only, without buildings. The sheet's scale bar and the initials of the surveyor with the date April 20, 1905 are printed in this strip.
notes: Placed from three hand-picked points (Elberon Avenue / Main Street, Allen Avenue / Main Street, Grassmere Avenue at the railroad) and one detected railroad crossing (Allen Avenue). Low confidence.
New York and Long Branch Railroad (today the North Jersey Coast Line) with passenger station; East Jersey Coast Company line laid 1898.
Dated P.H. 4/20/05.
